### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.surround

### Question

Suppose I have the following excerpt of text:

```
objects = [["foo", "bar", "baz"]]
```

My goal is to replace the outer square brackets with curly brackets. One option is to put my cursor at the beginning of the list and to type: `srb}`, which produces the desired output:

```
objects = {["foo", "bar", "baz"]}
```
However, two other approaches, which I had _thought_ would accomplish the same thing, do not, and I'm not totally sure why they do not.

Approach 1: I place my cursor somewhere within the list. I then highlight the text object around which I am looking to replace the brackets by typing `vab`. Then, I type `sr}`. However, this produces the following output:

```
objects = [}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}}]
```

Approcah 2: The operation `sa` supports using textobjects such as `iw` and `aw` instead of `w`, which is useful if the cursor is not located at the beginning of the text object. I thought that a similar approach might be useful for this task. However, if I type `srab}`, I observe the following output:

```
objects = [["foo", "b(r", "b)z"]]
```
Clearly, the command treated the character "a" as the surrounding character, and replaced it with the default bracket symbol.

I would love to could get some clarity as to why neither of these approaches work. Thanks!

comment_data.body:
Hello @julienberman,

Thanks for the questions!

If you place the cursor somewhere in the list, the following does the trick: `2srb}`

In your first approach, you intend to use `surround replace` in visual mode. However, replace is only active in normal mode. As a consequence, when typing `sr}`, the `s` is ignored, and `r}` replaces all characters in the visual selection with `}`. You can test this by only typing `r}` instead of `sr}`.

From the module description of `mini.surround`:

```help
Features:
- Actions (text editing actions are dot-repeatable out of the box and
  respect |[count]|) with configurable mappings:
    - Add surrounding with `sa` (in visual mode or on motion).
    - Delete surrounding with `sd`.
    - Replace surrounding with `sr`.
    - Find surrounding with `sf` or `sF` (move cursor right or left).
    - Highlight surrounding with `sh`.
```

Notice that "visual mode" is only mentioned in `Add`. I could not find an explicit mention of `Replace` only supporting normal mode. Perhaps the help could be more explicit in that regard.

Your second approach assumes that `replace` supports text objects, which is not the case. From the help:

```help
- Surrounding is identified by a single character as both "input" (in
  `delete` and `replace` start, `find`, and `highlight`) and "output" (in
  `add` and `replace` end):
```

reply_data.body:
> Notice that "visual mode" is only mentioned in `Add`. I could not find an explicit mention of `Replace` only supporting normal mode. Perhaps the help could be more explicit in that regard.

It is indeed not mentioned explicitly, mostly indeed because there are only mentions of Visual mode where it is supported. And also descriptions and example usages show that first step of "replace" action uses "Input surrounding", which means that surrounding will be searched relative to the cursor position. Making it work in Visual mode would require ignoring actual visual selection, which is somewhat confusing.
